bullets: eEwTOkVPoFM game 3 of 7 (video t=662.8-818.5s, in-game clock unreadable all video): a win over an Electro Giant / Graveyard beatdown deck with Goblin Cage, Inferno Dragon, Bowler and Baby Dragon. Both enemy Princess Towers were ground down (left 4858 to 768 HP by t=778s, right 4858 to 644 HP by t=812s) with no tower lost - "Very nice win... Perfect game" (t=812-815s).

The damage came entirely from stacked cheap threats, never one big push: Goblin Barrel plus Wall Breakers layered one second apart (t=695.5/695.7s), and Magic Archer chip from the river that took about 1700 HP off the left tower by itself at t=702-706s - "Look at all that magic archer chip. Beautiful."

Ronin is the flex slot, not the win condition. Ryley called it "a really weak card in this matchup" (t=707s), used it only as a defensive mini-tank at row 14, and refused the Ronin-plus-Wall-Breakers bridge rush at t=762-765s in favour of an opposite-lane Ronin with split Wall Breakers.

Defence is spirits first, spells second, building last: Fire Spirit and Ice Spirit blocked the Bowler (t=712.7s, t=724.6s), Royal Delivery answered a misplaced Inferno Dragon (t=791.8s), and the Bomb Tower stayed in hand for 125 seconds until the Electro Giant appeared - "let's just early bomb tower" (t=790s).

Spirit ordering is a stated technique in this deck: "Let's fire spirit low so we can go for a high ice spirit. So then the fire spirit is the spirit that will damage his tower cuz the fire spirit does more damage than the ice spirit" (t=748-754s).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers are the win conditions and both exist to bait the opponent's small spell and splash, backed by 1-elixir spirits and a defensive building rather than a tank.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck runs two cheap, spell-baiting win conditions - Goblin Barrel and Wall Breakers - and layers them so a single Log, Bowler or Cage answer can never cover both; in this match Ryley threw them one second apart at t=695.5s and again split them across lanes at t=764-769s. Magic Archer provides the deck's real damage engine, chipping from the river through anything in the arrow's line while the opponent invests behind (about 1700 HP of tower at t=702-706s). Defence is deliberately cheap and reactive: Ice Spirit and Fire Spirit block heavy hitters like the Bowler for 1 elixir, Royal Delivery erases misplaced support such as an Inferno Dragon, and the Bomb Tower is saved for the one card that actually needs it - a heavy tank like the Electro Giant. Ronin is the deck's swing slot, an excellent parry mini-tank against slow melee heavy hitters but, as Ryley says at t=707s, "a really weak card in this matchup" when the opponent defends with ranged and air units.
